### Axiom offsets, in one animation

<p align="center"><img src="{{fig:axiom_arrows_qwen3.5-2b.gif}}" alt="Pairs of group-like structures that differ in one axiom, drawn as 3-D arrows that slide to one common origin; Qwen3.5-2B left, its random-init twin right" width="720"></p>

- **What you see:** the 13 group-like structures (magma, unital magma, quasigroup, loop, semigroup, monoid, group, and the commutative versions of all but the unital magma) in the top-3 principal components of Qwen3.5-2B (left) and of its random-init twin (right), at the preregistered layer. One axiom at a time, every pair of structures that differ only in that axiom becomes an arrow, for example monoid → commutative monoid and group → abelian group for commutativity. The arrows then slide to one common origin, so you can see whether they point the same way.
- **What to notice:** in the trained model the commutativity arrows form one bundle. Their offset consistency, the mean cosine between the {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.commutative.n_pairs}} difference vectors in the full residual stream, is {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.commutative.consistency:.2f}}. The twin's is {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b__random.group_like.offsets.commutative.consistency:.2f}}, and random pairs of the same structures exceed {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.commutative.null95:.2f}} only 5% of the time. Associativity behaves the same way ({{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.associative.consistency:.2f}}, twin {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b__random.group_like.offsets.associative.consistency:.2f}}). Identity ({{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.identity.consistency:.2f}}) and divisibility ({{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.divisible.consistency:.2f}}) form looser bundles.
- **But mostly word form (audit):** five of the six arrows add the literal word "commutative", and the same six heads with a made-up modifier, X → zorbic X, give {{num:mvp.lexical.qwen3.5-2b.nonce_modifier.zorbic.trained.consistency:.2f}}. Character 3-grams of the names, with no model, give {{num:mvp.lexical.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.char3.commutative.consistency:.2f}} for commutativity and {{num:mvp.lexical.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.char3.associative.consistency:.2f}} for associativity. What survives the word-form controls is an associativity direction ({{fact:axiom_beyond_lexical.associative}}) and a "commutative" direction that also predicts abelian group − group, which shares no word with it ({{fact:abelian_transfer}}).
- **Caveat:** three principal components can hide or exaggerate parallelism, so the statistic is computed in the full space, never from this picture. In Qwen3.5-2B only {{fact:holm_axioms.qwen3.5-2b}} survive Holm correction; {{fact:holm_axioms_not.qwen3.5-2b}} are significant before correction only (the scorecard below has every model). Step-by-step static explainer: [`axioms_explainer_qwen3.5-2b.png`](reports/figures/axioms_explainer_qwen3.5-2b.png). [Interactive: how the test works](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-axiom-how), and [the lattice in 3-D](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-lattice).

## Highlights

*Every "n of 5" count below is computed from the results files (fact placeholders in `reports/readme_top_template.md`).*

**Positive results.** Each model is compared with its random-init twin (same architecture and tokenizer, no learning) and, since the [independent audit](reports/audit_lexical.md), with three baselines built from the names alone, without context: their spelling (character 3-grams, a bag of words) and the model's own context-free token embeddings.
- **Math fields form a map.** Field centroids from {{num:mvp.map_fields.qwen3.5-2b.math_primary.n_fields}} fields correlate with how often mathematicians cross-list papers between those fields on arXiv. This was the primary preregistered hypothesis (H-A1). It holds beyond the twin in {{fact:field_map_beats_twin}}, every random-init twin is near zero or below, and it exceeds all three name-only baselines in {{fact:field_beyond_lexical}} (Qwen3.5-2B: ρ = {{num:mvp.map_fields.qwen3.5-2b.math_primary.rsa.trained:.2f}}; the names' character 3-grams: {{num:mvp.lexical.qwen3.5-2b.field_map.rsa.char3:.2f}}, not significant; the context-free token embeddings: {{fact:lexical_field_range.layer0_bag}}, a weak map significant in {{fact:lexical_field_significant.layer0_bag}}). In Qwen3.5-2B, the only model run against the fastText and text-embedding baselines, the map is stronger than in fastText word vectors and about as strong as in a dedicated text-embedding model ([Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B)).
- **The space chain is ordered**: T0 ⊃ T1 ⊃ Hausdorff ⊃ … ⊃ Banach ⊃ Hilbert space. The full preregistered test (Robinson score and leave-one-out order, Holm-corrected, above the twin) holds in {{fact:chain_ordered.space_chain}}; spelling baselines do not order it, and it stays ordered within its metric block (metrizable … Hilbert) in {{fact:space_block.1}}.
- **Axiom offsets beyond word form, suggestive only.** An associativity direction exceeds every word-form baseline in {{fact:axiom_beyond_lexical.associative}}, and the "commutative" direction predicts abelian group − group in {{fact:abelian_transfer}}.
  - *How the test works:* for each axiom, take every pair of structures that differ only in that axiom, subtract their representations, and measure how parallel these difference vectors are (mean pairwise cosine in the full residual stream) against random pairs of the same structures. Step-by-step figure: [`axioms_explainer_qwen3.5-2b.png`]({{fig:axioms_explainer_qwen3.5-2b}}).
- **Concrete ↔ abstract is the top principal axis** of math-concept space in Qwen3.5-2B; pure ↔ applied is the second. Abstraction is rated by three LLM judges from other model families.

**Negative and null results:**
- **Most of the axiom geometry is word form (audit).** Difference vectors between structures that differ in one axiom are more parallel than random pairs (Holm-significant for associativity in {{fact:axiom_holm.associative}} and commutativity in {{fact:axiom_holm.commutative}}), but the names' character 3-grams alone pass the same test for all four axioms, and adding an irrelevant real word (X → wooden X) or a made-up one (X → zorbic X) is about as consistent as X → commutative X; "commutative" is the most consistent of the three in {{fact:nonce_above}}. Identity's offset comes from two pairs of pairs that repeat the same head-noun change with and without "commutative".
- **The ring chain's order is not established beyond its head nouns (audit).** It passes the preregistered test in {{fact:chain_ordered.ring_chain}}, but its names end in contiguous blocks of head nouns (rng | ring | … domain | field), clusters of head nouns without any order pass the same test in up to {{num:mvp.lexical.block_only_simulation.2.reject_rate:.0%}} of simulations, and the six "… domain" items are ordered among themselves in {{fact:ring_within}}.
- **Lie groups and other group objects: word form (audit).** The analogies topological group − group ≈ topological space − set and Lie group − topological group ≈ smooth manifold − topological space clear their null in {{fact:parallelograms}}, but the names' character 3-grams are more parallel than the models (models above every word-form baseline: {{fact:group_objects_beyond}}).
- **Angles are not a circle.** In {{fact:angles_far}}, "330 degrees" is farther from "0 degrees" than neighbouring angles are from each other (closure ratio {{fact:angles_closure_range}}), and the angles are ordered like a line (line ρ {{fact:angles_range.line_rho}}; twins {{fact:twin_angles_range.line_rho}}). This falsifies one of our preregistered predictions. Numbers lie on a generalized helix whose periodic parts need not show in the first two principal components ([Kantamneni & Tegmark 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00873)), so we also looked in all 10 planes of the top 5 components. That test was post-hoc, but specified in writing and committed before it ran ([addendum](reports/prereg_addendum_3d.md)). Models with a significant closed cycle of angles there: {{fact:angles_closed_plane}}.
- **The map is not a clean hierarchy (H-A2).** Under the preregistered measure (cophenetic correlation with a five-branch super-tree), the trained models beat shuffled trees in {{fact:beats_shuffled_trees}}, but beat their random-init twins in {{fact:hierarchy_beats_twin}}. By cophenetic correlation, a model is more tree-like than a Gaussian cloud with the same spectrum in {{fact:gaussian_more_treelike.coph_c}}; relative Gromov δ, a second tree measure, does call {{fact:gaussian_more_treelike.delta_rel}} more tree-like than that cloud, but by δ, {{fact:twin_delta_rel_lower}} are more tree-like still ({{fact:delta_rel_range.random_init}} vs {{fact:delta_rel_range.trained}}), so δ gives no support beyond the twin.
- **Over a trillion tokens of math pretraining did not sharpen the map.** Qwen2.5-Math vs its base ([Qwen2.5-Math report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12122)) shows no detectable difference (H-A3).
- **Specificity to mathematics is untested.** Biology, chemistry, geology and astronomy topics cluster by field more strongly than most random sets of four math fields, in {{fact:control_beats_most_math_subsets}}. But these controls are whole sciences, not sub-fields, so the comparison confounds domain with granularity and cannot show that the map is unspecific to mathematics (audit).
- **The causal test was inconclusive.** The ring chain failed the accuracy gate. For the space chain, noise in the chain subspace hurt accuracy only slightly more than random-subspace noise, and only at the larger noise scales.
- **The positive control (days and months as circles) failed our preregistered full-space criterion, and replicates only partly with post-hoc tests.**
  - The full-space criterion fails because line ρ exceeds circle ρ for days in {{fact:line_beats_circle.days}} and for months in {{fact:line_beats_circle.months}}.
  - In the top-2 principal-component plane, where [Engels et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14860) show their raw-activation circles, days go round in perfect order in {{fact:top2_cycle_perfect.days}} and months in {{fact:top2_cycle_perfect.months}}. But that score also rewards an open arc.
  - Counting only loops that close in their plane (the same addendum), days close in the top-2 plane in {{fact:closes_top2.days}}. Months close in a lower plane ({{fact:lower_planes.months}}; p < .05 each, unadjusted) in {{fact:closes_lower_plane.months}}.
  - A closed months loop also appears in {{fact:twin_closes.months}}, so this test is not fully specific. All outcomes are reported.

**Methods findings.** Before touching LLM data, we simulated partial regression on distance matrices. When the nuisance matrix is only a proxy of a confounder, it rejects true nulls far too often. That is why the field-map tests are paired contrasts with concept-bootstrap CIs: H-A1 and H-A2 against the random-init twin, H-A3 between Qwen2.5-Math and its base model. The audit then showed that a random-init twin does not control for word form, because it can scramble even exact word composition (strongly in the Qwen3.5 twins): studies of concept geometry need name-only baselines too.
